title: Anthropic Declares War on Microsoft and Google: Launches Claude Sheets and Video Call Assistant, Making a Full Foray into Smart Office Software
excerpt: As its U.S. stock market listing draws nearer, leading AI company Anthropic is accelerating its push into a new commercial battleground. At its latest industry
content_html:
As its U.S. stock market listing draws nearer, leading AI company Anthropic is accelerating its push into a new commercial battleground. At its latest industry event, Anthropic unveiled a series of new tools deeply integrated into everyday office scenarios, formally launching head-on competition in Microsoft and Google’s core office territory.

Full-Scale Push Into the Intelligent Office Ecosystem, Multiple Major Tools Unveiled Together

To bring powerful large-model capabilities closer to users’ daily workflows, Anthropic’s newly released feature matrix covers multiple core office scenarios. The most notable is a spreadsheet service called Claude Sheets. In terms of its core functional form, it is highly similar to mainstream offerings such as Microsoft Excel and Google Sheets, but the biggest difference is that Anthropic’s native AI capabilities are deeply built into its foundation, enabling it to directly handle complex data analysis and spreadsheet tasks through intelligent conversation.

In addition to the spreadsheet service, the release also includes a video call assistant for everyday collaboration and a powerful data dashboard tool, comprehensively covering enterprise users’ daily office and data management needs.

Paid Beta Launches First, Going Head-to-Head With Tech Giants Ahead of IPO

Regarding the product’s concrete rollout and commercialization pace, Anthropic officially announced that this new suite of office tools will first be made fully available to paying users in beta form.

Industry analysts point out that at the critical moment when the company is sprinting toward an IPO, Anthropic’s launch of an office suite directly targeting Microsoft Office and Google Workspace not only further broadens its own path to commercialization, but also marks that its competition with traditional tech giants such as Microsoft and Google in the enterprise AI services field has officially entered a fully heated stage.
